To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measurement of the coupling structure of a Higgs-like boson in the weak bosons fusion channel is possible with a precision of about 10%, and that the coupling structure of the standard model Higgs can be excluded at a level of 2σ at mH = 120 GeV with 30 fb−1 of data and at a level of more than 5 σ at mH =160 GeV with 100 fb-1.

purely anomalous Higgs couplings are expected be excluded at a level corresponding to a confidence level of 2σ or higher for mH=120 GeV and more than 4σ for mH=160 GeV from 30  fb−1 of data, and that a measurement of a CP even coupling in addition to a standard model coupling with a precision of 20% at mH= 120 GeV and better than 10% at mH = 160 GeV
the measurement of the Higgs boson self-coupling in the weak bosons fusion channel is possible with high precision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prospects for the measurement and the determination of the tensor structure in the H→W+W− vertex using weak boson fusion at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) with the ATLAS experiment.
the prospects for a measurement of a CP even coupling contribution to the vertex between a Higgs bosons and two weak gauge vectors in weak boson scattering.
the prospects for measuring the structure of the vertex of a Higgs to weak gauge boson vertex in weak boson scattering with the ATLAS experiment at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prospects for the measurement are excellent.
the prospects for the measurement with the ATLAS experiment are very good.
a measurement with a precision of 10% or better of the tensor structure in a measurement of the HWW vertex is expected to be possible in the weak bosons fusion channel at the LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the prospects for a measurement of a purely anomalous Higgs-gauge coupling in weak boson production are excellent, but the measurement of a CP even contribution to the Higgs-gauge vertex is challenging.

the measurement of the Higgs boson couplings to weak gauge boson is possible with a precision of about 10% at the LHC with 30 fb of data, if the Higgs bosons are produced in the weak bosons fusion process.
the prospects for the measurement are good and that the measurement of a CP even coupling in addition to a standard model coupling is feasible with the ATLAS experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of the CP even coupling is possible at a level that allows to distinguish it from the standard model at a 5σ level at mH=140 GeV.
the Higgs coupling to weak bosons can be probed at the LHC with high precision.
the weak boson-fusion production of a Higgs particle at the LHC will be a very powerful probe of the tensor structure at the vertex coupling a Higgs particle to weak gauge boson pairs.
